metadata.title: Results from TALIS Starting Strong 2024: Japan

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This Japan participant note reports descriptive survey results from TALIS Starting Strong 2024, based on questionnaires administered to ECEC staff and setting leaders. The note does not specify the use of student/sampling weights or replicate-weight procedures (e.g., BRR/jackknife) in the excerpt provided, so weight application cannot be confirmed from the text. For analysts using the underlying TALIS Starting Strong 2024 database, estimates should follow the survey’s complex sampling design guidance (stratification/clustering) and apply the provided sampling weights at the relevant level (staff and/or setting) to obtain representative estimates within each participating country/subnational entity. Because this document is a descriptive results note rather than a model-based ML analysis, the key requirement is correct weighted estimation for proportions and differences, not PV-based scaling or ML-specific weighting.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD participant note summarizes descriptive findings from TALIS Starting Strong 2024 for Japan, based on self-reports from ECEC staff and setting leaders in pre-primary settings (ISCED level 02). The survey collects information on staff and leader demographics, working hours, professional development, contract modalities, practices with children and families, and well-being, job satisfaction, and career intentions. Indicators are reported as percentages (and some percentage-point differences) for topics such as time spent in direct contact with children, staff education levels, professional development needs and participation (including job-embedded training and collaborative learning), family engagement practices, and collaboration with health/social services. Workforce retention and stress are summarized via leaders’ reports of staff shortages/absences and staff reports of job satisfaction, perceived value, and reasons for potentially leaving. The excerpt does not provide model-based performance metrics or PV/missing-data procedures, and it cautions that estimates may be affected by non-response bias.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is a descriptive results note for an OECD large-scale survey (TALIS Starting Strong 2024) rather than an empirical ML/predictive study. Consequently, there is no student-level analytic sample size, no PV-based achievement outcome, no ML algorithm evaluation, and no model performance metrics to extract. The excerpt also does not specify weighting variables or missing-data handling procedures, which are typically documented in the full TALIS Starting Strong 2024 technical report/database documentation rather than in a participant highlights note.
